newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal net financing needs 1997 down 35 pct.
newsitem.headline: Portugal net financing needs 1997 down 35 pct.

text.p: The Portuguese state's net financing needs in 1997 will fall 35 percent to 393 billion escudos from 603 billion escudos this year, according to the state budget.
The budget, which was made public on Tuesday after being sent to parliament, sees the Treasury issuing 250 billion escudos of foreign debt, including 26 billion of amortizations.
Net foreign debt issued will be 241 billion this year, the budget document said. Total state debt was 70.7 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1996 against 71.5 percent in 1995.
The Treasury will issue a total 775.2 billion escudos of fixed-rate bonds (OT), including 242.6 billion escudos of amortizations. No figures were immediately available for 1996.
Issues of Treasury bills were seen at 1,357 billion escudos, with 1,333 billion of amortizations.
Some 855 billion escudos of old variable-rate bonds, known as FIPs, will be amortized. The Treasury is no longer issuing this paper.
